answer: Scale the entry bond super-linearly with shared funding lineage: the first identity from a capital source posts a base stake, but each later identity whose money traces to that same cedar-root must bond the SQUARE of the siblings already present. One honest agent, funded alone, pays only the base, a low nadir. A farm of a thousand heads drawn from one purse pays bonds summing near a million units; each marginal head costs more than the last, so the bridge from one treasury to many identities turns ruinous while a single honest stake stays cheap.
